request: Do task P3-18 in docs/PLAN-PHASE-3.md: 'Offline states, and a test that actually goes offline'. Follow docs/AGENT-WORKFLOW.md and read the docs in the task's Reads column (UX-PRINCIPLES.md section 7, ARCHITECTURE.md section Progressive enhancement and offline) before changing anything. A saved garden must work with no connection; a plant or a tile that is not cached says 'needs connection' rather than guessing; user-visible strings only in src/i18n/. Add a Playwright test that drives the app with the network cut. The work is done when the phase's acceptance criteria hold: npm run check, pwsh scripts/verify.ps1 and the Playwright suite (npm run test:e2e) each pass, as separate gates, as in CI.

task.title: Refactor ResultsSection to tolerate per-shard failure and render 'needs connection' for uncached shards
task.action: Replace the Promise.all over all catalogue shards in ResultsSection.tsx with per-shard error handling (Promise.allSettled or individual try/catch). Collect plants from successful shards into the results array. For each failed shard, render a 'needs connection' placeholder for the plants in that shard using the i18n key added in task 1. The component should branch on DataError.code === 'offline-unavailable' to show the specific offline message, and fall back to the generic loadError for other failure types. This is the most significant structural change: it enables partial rendering where cached plants show normally and uncached ones say 'needs connection'.
task.motivation: ResultsSection.tsx:78-79 loads all shards with Promise.all; a single shard failure sets loadError=true and the entire results section shows a generic error. P3-18 requires per-item availability: 'a plant or a tile that is not cached says needs connection rather than guessing'. The current all-or-nothing pattern cannot express 'plant A loaded, plant B needs connection'.

dod.statement: TypeScript compilation succeeds with the refactored ResultsSection
dod.rubric: Pass only if the code and its tests show this: TypeScript compilation succeeds with the refactored ResultsSection. Cite the test that proves it, by file and line, and the code it exercises. A claim with no test behind it fails.

dod.statement: The change introduces no new untrusted-input, secret-handling or authorisation weakness
dod.rubric: Trace each new or modified input path to its use. Pass only if untrusted input is validated before use, secrets are neither logged nor returned, and authorisation checks fail closed.

dod.statement: No wait, retry or lock this change adds can hang, deadlock or spin without bound
dod.rubric: Follow every wait, retry and lock acquisition the change adds or modifies. Pass only on a bounded-time demonstration: a named test that drives the contended or failing path to completion inside a stated wall-clock bound, with the measured time quoted. Reading the code is not a demonstration. Fail if a retry loop has neither a delay nor an attempt ceiling, if a lock is taken without a timeout, or if a failure path returns to the same wait with nothing changed.

dod.statement: The change follows the conventions of the files it touches and introduces no duplicated logic that already exists in the codebase
dod.rubric: Compare against the surrounding code. Pass only if naming, structure and error handling match local convention, and no copied block duplicates an existing helper.

task.decision_note: approved by the harness within the granted envelope
